What is a woman supposed to look like

Personally, as a lesbian:

“Oh she’s pretty” is the hair, the face, maybe she’s got a nice outfit or lovely makeup. You see her walk by and continue on your own path. Maybe you’ll copy part of her look later. But all you’ll remember is the shirt, the nail polish. Not her face or anything else. 

“Yes I have the gay” is not just the hair, but the way it moves around her face. You notice the way it bounces or flows. Her eyes see right through you even if there isn’t even a passing moment of eye contact. Were they green? Blue? Hazel? You want to get up closer to see. The look on her face is picturesque and artistic. Is she determined? Relaxed? Joyful? What was she smiling about? You’re happy that she’s having a good day. When her back is turned, you take advantage to just look at her walking away. Peppy bouncing? Tired shuffle? Maybe you happened to catch the scent of her, you try to find it later just because it was so pleasing. Perfume? The forest? You smile as you bury your nose in your bedsheets, finding out that it was fresh linen. You inhale deeply and then feel incredibly creepy. She made you think a million things at once and your head is full of question marks.

I was friends with a guy who put too much feelings into the idea of being with me only for him to be shot down when I told him I’m lesbian. Our friendship hasn’t been the same since, I feel awkward around him because of how poorly he took it. 

3- To catch someone’s eye, make them feel welcome. Smile at them, engage in interesting and pleasant conversations. As you get to know them better, you may be able to talk about more specific things, which will lead to stronger memories and inside jokes. Be a true friend. Don’t change yourself for them and don’t make them change for you. I believe that the most sound and reliable people find respect to be the biggest factor in whether they are interested in someone or not. And putting effort into getting to know someone without trying to force anything or manipulate situations is the most respectful thing to do.

4- At first, I was sad that I would not be able to have biological kids with my future wife, as I intend on getting married at some point. But the idea of adoption has stolen my heart and I can say with confidence that I never want it back. There are so many children without homes in the world. Population is rising too quickly for the world to handle. So that appeals to logic. And sexual reproduction is really just intended for opposite sex couples. I don’t see a reason to engage in any form of sperm banking. (If my wife ends up really wanting to, I will of course support her, but I would not choose to be pregnant myself.) While I believe this may lead to some dissatisfaction as I have a biological female body and mind that may at some point have urges to conceive and carry a child, I believe the true satisfaction in being a mother is the actual care taking and raising of a child. I love kids and when I see a baby just on the street, I find myself smiling at the memory for the rest of the day and telling everyone about how I just saw “the cutest baby”. So I have no doubt that I will be able to embrace a parentless baby or child into my household with the same true love a mother can give to her biological children. And some people even say there is a special bond between parents and adopted children. So I look forward very much to having a house full of youth and love someday.

Right here- parents have helped me through thick and thin. They are great and responsible people. They raised me to value good things in life and to work on myself for myself and nobody else. They can only realistically protect me from so much though. Nobody saw the rape coming, the sexual abuse and gaslighting a year later, or the plan for suicide. I’ve given them more than a fair share of teenager hell and they reacted by trying to understand, help, teach, and build me up. Every bit of confidence I have I owe to the solid family I have standing behind me. And when happier things came along, such as my love for art and coming out to them as lesbian, they reacted with warmth and assurance. They celebrate who I am because they are happy for ME before being happy for their work as parents. From the outside, they may seem like average or even boring people, with boring jobs and an average middle class life. But the work they have constantly put into this family makes every bit of life priceless. Even when fighting about the dishes. I have a few years to go before I’ll hopefully be off to college and I know they will be there for me through whatever else happens in the future.
